$comment: The crate half of the architecture map, read by `cargo xtask arch-map`. Every crate of the target graph is listed, planned ones included, so dependency direction is fixed before any code exists. A layer may depend only on the layers in its mayDependOn; a crate only on its allowedInternalDeps. A crate path must sit under one of its layer's dirs. Adapters never reach mechanics: ADR-0018 holds by construction.

core.description: pure, no I/O, unchanged on wasm32 and native

ports.description: the only route to I/O: async traits and the error taxonomy

adapters.description: translate HTTP and MCP to ops, and nothing else

mechanics.description: port implementations over a concrete store

bindings.description: composition roots: wasm-bindgen, workers-rs, the native daemon

tooling.description: repository tooling, test utilities and fuzz targets, never shipped

whiteboard-det.description: JS-compatible number formatting, pinned math, UTF-16 helpers, seeded randomness, ordered collections

allowedThirdParty.libm: fdlibm sin and cos, pure Rust and no_std, so they run unchanged on wasm32 and native; pinned exactly because canvas-render's det-math.ts is held to its bits

whiteboard-log.description: RFC 5424 levels, records, sinks and the fields-first logging macro

whiteboard-model.description: serde types generated from contracts/model plus the invariants a schema cannot express

whiteboard-facet-engine.description: facet registry, write validation, compat chain, derived forms, theme tokens

whiteboard-scene.description: the scene vocabulary and the contribution traits

whiteboard-codec.description: OKF Markdown, JSON Canvas and OCIF serialize and parse

whiteboard-search.description: tokenizer, BM25 ranking, snippets, searchable text

whiteboard-plugin-visual.description: the bundled visual plugin as an ordinary contribution implementer

whiteboard-edge-routing.description: side choice, anchors, grid search, crossings, jumps, rounding, label anchor, budget, route cache

allowedThirdParty.serde: the derive the generated contract types use (contracts/geometry); no I/O, builds unchanged on wasm32 and native

whiteboard-canvas-render.description: composer, typesetter, line breaking, theme, SVG backend, sceneDigest, references

whiteboard-crdt.description: the loro bridge, workspace tree, file references, text-limit judge

whiteboard-history.description: checkpoint scheduling, version retention, frontier encoding

whiteboard-workspace-index.description: the document index over a workspace tree

whiteboard-reference-graph.description: per-document reference facts and the backlink aggregate

whiteboard-ports.description: async I/O traits (stores, index, blobs, clock, id mint, scheduler, text measurement, fonts) and the error taxonomy

whiteboard-api-contracts.description: generated types for /api, sync frames, MCP tool I/O and the refusal enum

whiteboard-ops.description: every /api/v1 operation and MCP tool as a transport-neutral execute over ports; the tool table as data

whiteboard-http.description: an axum router over ops, mounted natively and on Workers

whiteboard-mcp.description: a transport-agnostic JSON-RPC dispatcher over the ops tool table

whiteboard-daemon-store.description: SQLite record store, fs blob store, versions, migrations, file GC, security stores, export

whiteboard-edge-store.description: Durable Object, D1 and R2 stores

whiteboard-wasm.description: the wasm-bindgen cdylib for the browser and Node; render and full artifacts by feature

allowedThirdParty.wasm-bindgen: the JS boundary itself; pinned = to the wasm-bindgen-cli that post-processes the artifact
allowedThirdParty.serde_json: the OKF exports' document wire: a frontmatter value is arbitrary nested data, which no flat typed array holds. Pure Rust, no I/O, runs unchanged on wasm32 and native; deny.toml already bans unbounded_depth and arbitrary_precision, so the 128-level recursion limit is part of the entry's depth cap

whiteboard-worker.description: the workers-rs app: router, MCP over HTTP, edge store, alarms

whiteboard-daemon.description: the native daemon binary: UDS server, MCP stdio, native-messaging host, PNG export

xtask.description: repository tasks: codegen, architecture map, wasm import scan, the core crates' cross-target tests, size and unsafe ledgers, fuzz registry, release gates (harden-check, repro-check, dist)

allowedThirdParty.serde: deserializes the architecture map and the size ledger
allowedThirdParty.serde_json: reads cargo metadata and the checked-in JSON ledgers
allowedThirdParty.wasmparser: reads a wasm artifact's import section for the core import scan
allowedThirdParty.object: reads a native binary's ELF headers, segments and dynamic table for harden-check (read-only, std + elf features only)

whiteboard-proptest.description: the one proptest prelude (QR-14b/d/e): the case budget, an unseeded runner, regressions beside the property, the reachability floor; a dev-dependency only

allowedThirdParty.proptest: the property runner (QR-14); std only, no fork or timeout, so the same property runs natively and on wasm32 under Node
allowedThirdParty.getrandom: wasm32 only, with wasm_js: each run's fresh seed from the host's crypto.getRandomValues, since no seed is pinned (QR-14d)

whiteboard-native-fixture.description: a minimal native binary built with the dist-native profile, so the release gates (harden-check, repro-check, cargo-auditable, third-party notices) run against a real artifact until whiteboard-daemon replaces it

whiteboard-fuzz.description: cargo-fuzz targets, one per untrusted-input entry (OKF/JSON Canvas/OCIF parsers, sync frames, HTTP and MCP JSON-RPC, loro import, wasm-boundary JSON, font files). Nightly toolchain only (libFuzzer, sanitizers), so it is a workspace of its own, excluded from the root one; its library half builds on stable to replay committed regressions

allowedThirdParty.libfuzzer-sys: the libFuzzer driver cargo-fuzz links each target against; optional, so the target bodies build on stable
